what_its_for: Pemetrexed is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of lung cancer, including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and malignant pleural mesothelioma (a cancer that affects the lining of the lungs). Your doctor may use it alone or combined with other cancer medicines.
how_to_take: Pemetrexed is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into your vein by a healthcare professional in a clinic or hospital. You will NOT take this medicine at home by yourself. Each infusion takes about 10 minutes. Before and during your treatment, you will also need to take folic acid (a vitamin) by mouth every day and receive vitamin B12 injections every 9 weeks. Your doctor will also give you a steroid (like dexamethasone) the day before, the day of, and the day after each infusion to help prevent skin rashes.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your body size (height and weight). A typical treatment cycle is once every 21 days (every 3 weeks). You will receive your infusion on Day 1 of each cycle. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have side effects or kidney problems. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing schedule.
missed_dose: Since this medicine is given by a healthcare provider, a missed dose is unlikely. However, if you miss or need to reschedule your appointment, call your doctor or cancer care team right away to set up a new appointment as soon as possible. Do not try to make up for a missed treatment on your own.
storage: You will not store this medicine at home. It is prepared and stored by healthcare professionals at the clinic or hospital. If you are given folic acid tablets or vitamin B12 supplements to take at home, store them at room temperature away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep all medicines out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve) around the time of your treatment without talking to your doctor first, as they can increase side effects. Avoid getting vaccinations with live vaccines during treatment without checking with your doctor. Avoid close contact with people who are sick or have infections, as this medicine can weaken your immune system. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child during treatment, as pemetrexed can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for several months after.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, chills, or signs of infection; unusual bleeding or bruising; severe mouth sores that make it hard to eat or drink; severe diarrhea or vomiting; shortness of breath or chest pain; severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling; swelling of your face, lips, or throat; yellowing of the skin or eyes; dark urine or severe stomach pain; feeling very weak or dizzy; or little to no urination. These may be signs of a serious problem that needs immediate medical attention.
when_it_works: Pemetrexed works right away at the cellular level to slow or stop cancer cell growth, but it may take several weeks to months before you or your doctor can see the results through scans or tests. Your doctor will regularly check how well the medicine is working with blood tests and imaging scans. Everyone responds differently, so keep all your follow-up appointments.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor will check your kidney function before each dose. If your kidneys are not working well, your dose may be reduced or treatment may be delayed. Older adults (65 and older): You can still receive this medicine, but you may be more sensitive to side effects and will be monitored closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm your baby. Do not breastfeed while receiving pemetrexed and for at least one week after your last dose. Children: The safety and effectiveness of pemetrexed in children have not been well established; talk to your doctor.
